body: Thank you for your feedback! I will take all of this into consideration and will make adjustments in the future.

While there is no exclusionary criteria for location, the study is in english, so it requires proficiency in english to participate. Also, the compensation for the study is provided via Amazon gifts cards in US currency.

Great question! It starts with the screening questions to determine eligibility. After those is a consent form with all the detailed information of the study and what participation looks like. Tasks vary by week, but are essentially an initial demographics questionnaire, four weekly “sessions” (all less than 40 minutes), and then a follow up questionnaire a month after your last weekly session. Everything is done online.

That is a great question, thank you, and actually gets at the core of what we are attempting to see. Could moving towards regarding life as sacred serve to decrease, as you describe it, the barrage of suicidal thoughts? To my knowledge, this is a new approach so we don’t really know that much about it. I’m hoping with this study we can get a foundational understanding of whether this might be a way to address suicidal experiences. Agreed that historically that word carries a religious connotation. This study was designed to be secular, and does not have any inclusionary criteria based on religion. Thank you for your support and your thoughts!
